entries.requirement_text: The execution report shall be produced when the workflow fails or when cleanup after successful promotion fails. It shall distinguish completed stages from the failed stage and any pending stages not reached. The completion_status shall be failed for pre-promotion and indeterminate failures, and promoted-with-finalization-error when promotion committed but post-promotion cleanup failed. Under cleanup failure, the report shall record the promotion stage status as completed and the success-finalization stage status as failed with the cleanup failure reason in the errors array.

entries.requirement_text: The report `schema_version` shall be the constant string `1`. The `completion_status` shall be one of: `failed` (pre-promotion failure or indeterminate promotion) or `promoted-with-finalization-error` (promotion committed but post-promotion cleanup failed). The required `promotion_outcome` / `completion_status` combinations are: pre-promotion failure — `promotion_outcome` = `not-promoted` and `completion_status` = `failed`; indeterminate promotion — `promotion_outcome` = `indeterminate` and `completion_status` = `failed`; cleanup failure after committed promotion — `promotion_outcome` = `promoted` and `completion_status` = `promoted-with-finalization-error`. A `promoted-with-finalization-error` completion_status shall not be misreported as a pre-promotion failure; the repository is successfully promoted. Every required terminal outcome shall be representable using only the required fields, with no undeclared fields.

entries.requirement_text: When post-promotion cleanup fails after successful promotion, the execution report shall have completion_status promoted-with-finalization-error and promotion_outcome promoted. The report shall record the success-finalization stage status as failed with the cleanup failure reason in the errors array, and shall record the promotion stage status as completed. The execution report shall record the promoted destination path in the expected_destination field and shall not misreport the repository as unpromoted. Under cleanup failure, the execution report stages shall represent: promotion as completed, success-finalization as failed, and all prior stages as completed. The staging_root field shall identify the preserved staging transaction root used for diagnostics. The execution report and staging-state record shall agree on the request fingerprint, destination, and promotion outcome (both shall record promotion as promoted) and on the terminal result (both shall record success-finalization as failed); the two records must not disagree about promotion.

entries.requirement_text: The bounded local workflow has four terminal outcomes: pre-promotion failure (any required stage fails before promotion), promoted success (promotion commits and success-finalization completes), indeterminate promotion (rename outcome cannot be determined), and cleanup failure (promotion committed but post-promotion staging-root removal fails). Each terminal outcome has distinct diagnostic preservation, caller return, and retry-authorization rules defined by the governing workflow specification. The execution report and staging-state record shall record a mutually consistent terminal outcome: they shall agree on the request fingerprint, expected destination, promotion outcome, failed stage, and terminal result. Under cleanup failure, the staging-state record shall have: `current_stage` = `success-finalization`, `failed_stage` = `success-finalization`, `completed_stages` includes promotion (completed) and excludes success-finalization (not completed), `promotion_entered` = `true`, `promotion_outcome` = `promoted`, and `cleanup_failure` = non-empty diagnostic string.

entries.requirement_text: A cleanup failure after successful promotion is distinct from a pre-promotion failure: the repository is successfully promoted and must not be misreported as unpromoted. The workflow returns a promoted-with-finalization-error result. No automatic retry of the failed cleanup operation is authorized without external diagnosis. Under cleanup failure, `promotion_outcome` remains `promoted`; the `cleanup_failure` field records the failure reason. The execution report shall record `promotion_outcome` `promoted` and `completion_status` `promoted-with-finalization-error`, agreeing with the staging-state record so that both records together report the repository as promoted. The staging transaction root is preserved when accessible for diagnostics. The destination remains authoritative and must not be reported as absent or unpromoted.

entries.requirement_text: The `git_created` field shall be `true` when local Git initialization has completed inside `repository/`. The staging-state record must not claim `validation_completed` equal to `true` before the validation report has been successfully serialized and written. The staging-state record and the validation report shall share matching `request_fingerprint` and `repository_content_digest` values.

entries.requirement_text: The `cleanup_failure` field shall be a required nullable field that is always present in every staging-state record. When cleanup has not been attempted or when cleanup succeeds, `cleanup_failure` shall be `null`. When post-promotion staging-root removal fails after `promotion_outcome` is `promoted`, `cleanup_failure` shall be a non-empty diagnostic string describing the cleanup failure reason; the presence of a non-null `cleanup_failure` value does not change the promotion outcome. The deterministic serialized forms are: normal state — `"cleanup_failure": null`; cleanup-failure state — `"cleanup_failure": "<non-empty diagnostic string>"`. The canonical cleanup-failure staging-state is: `current_stage` = `success-finalization`, `failed_stage` = `success-finalization`, `completed_stages` includes `promotion` (completed) and does not include `success-finalization` (not completed), `promotion_entered` = `true`, `promotion_outcome` = `promoted`, and `cleanup_failure` = non-empty diagnostic string. No automatic rollback or retry of the failed cleanup operation is authorized.

entries.requirement_text: Every check in the profile must apply to one of the following scopes: request, source, material-manifest, repository-worktree, or git-state. entries.requirement_text: After all Phase 1 and Phase 2 checks are complete, report finalization is a deterministic ordered write operation that shall proceed in this exact order: (a) calculate the proposed overall_status (pass when every required Phase 1 and Phase 2 check has status passed, otherwise fail); (b) construct in memory a proposed final validation report carrying the proposed overall_status, the canonical request_fingerprint, and the expected repository_content_digest from the output.repository-digest-match check; (c) construct in memory a proposed final staging-state representation carrying validation_completed equal to true, validation_overall_status equal to the proposed overall_status, the canonical request_fingerprint, and the expected repository_content_digest; (d) validate the proposed staging-state representation against the product.staging-state schema in memory without writing it; (e) validate the proposed validation report against the validation-report schema in memory, verifying the request_fingerprint linkage, the repository_content_digest linkage, and check ordering and uniqueness; (f) serialize and write the finalized validation report atomically to transaction/validation-report.json; (g) serialize and write the finalized staging-state record atomically to transaction/staging-state.json; and (h) re-read or otherwise verify that the two durable records are mutually consistent, confirming they share the same request_fingerprint and repository_content_digest and that the staging-state validation_completed and validation_overall_status agree with the completed validation result. These postconditions are not ordinary profile checks; they are validation-component invariants enforced during report finalization before promotion. Any failure in steps (a) through (h) shall prevent promotion.

entries.requirement_text: The repository validation component shall execute two validation phases in order: Phase 1 (input and source) validates request schema, canonicalization, authority propagation, source repository, source commit, material-manifest schema, source paths (rejecting tree-valued entries), and key coverage. Phase 2 (staged repository and Git state) validates the complete staged repository at repository/ including output inventory (confirming no tree-valued material_index entries), copied files, direction evidence, generated templates, promoted records, provenance, handoff, content digest, Git branch, commit count, author identity, commit message, worktree cleanliness, and remote count. Staging-state record validation is not an ordinary Phase 1 or Phase 2 check; it is performed during report finalization as an ordered in-memory validation of the proposed staging-state representation before any record is written.

entries.requirement_text: After all Phase 1 and Phase 2 checks are recorded, the validation component shall perform report finalization as an ordered write operation: (a) calculate the proposed overall_status (pass when every required Phase 1 and Phase 2 check has status passed, otherwise fail); (b) construct and validate in memory a proposed final validation report and a proposed final staging-state representation carrying validation_completed equal to true, validation_overall_status equal to the proposed overall_status, the canonical request_fingerprint, and the expected repository_content_digest; (c) verify request_fingerprint linkage, repository_content_digest linkage, check ordering and uniqueness, and the completed report schema; (d) write the finalized validation report durably; (e) write the finalized staging-state record durably; and (f) verify that both durable records are mutually consistent (shared request_fingerprint and repository_content_digest, and staging-state validation_completed and validation_overall_status agreeing with the completed validation result). Promotion is permitted only when a finalized validation report and a finalized staging-state record both exist, both are durably written and mutually consistent, the report validates against its schema, every required Phase 1 and Phase 2 check has status passed, and overall_status is pass. The validation component shall not proceed to the promotion stage when any required Phase 1 or Phase 2 check has status failed, error, or skipped, or when report finalization (including any write or consistency-verification step) fails.

entries.requirement_text: The validation report shall not include a check that recursively validates the report itself. Fingerprint linkage, digest linkage, check ordering, check uniqueness, proposed staging-state validation, report schema validation, serialization, and the final durable-record consistency verification are not ordinary profile checks; they are validation-component postconditions enforced during report finalization before promotion. Report finalization is an ordered write operation: calculate the proposed overall result, construct and validate the proposed validation report and proposed staging-state representation in memory, write the finalized validation report durably, write the finalized staging-state record durably, and verify both durable records are mutually consistent. The staging-state record must not claim validation_completed equal to true before the validation report has been successfully written. Report finalization failure (including staging-state schema failure, fingerprint mismatch, digest mismatch, validation-status mismatch, linkage mismatch, ordering violation, report schema failure, serialization error, or failure to durably write both records consistently) shall be recorded as a pre-promotion failure and shall prevent promotion.

entries.requirement_text: Promotion to the declared destination shall occur only after report finalization completes in its ordered write sequence (calculate the proposed overall result; construct and validate the proposed validation report and proposed staging-state representation in memory; write the finalized validation report durably; write the finalized staging-state record durably; re-read or verify that both durable records are mutually consistent), both the finalized validation report and the finalized staging-state record at transaction/staging-state.json are durably written and mutually consistent, and the finalized validation report's overall_status is pass. The staging-state record must validate against the product.staging-state schema, its request_fingerprint must match the canonical request fingerprint, its repository_content_digest must match the expected digest, and its validation_completed and validation_overall_status must agree with the completed validation result. Promotion must not begin when only one of the two records has been durably written. When overall_status is fail (because a required Phase 1 or Phase 2 check has status failed, error, or skipped, or because report finalization including any write or consistency-verification step failed), or when the two durable records cannot be written consistently, promotion shall not occur and the workflow shall fail before promotion, leaving the staging transaction root in its pre-promotion state for diagnostics.

entries.requirement_text: After successful promotion, the cleanup order shall be: (1) confirm promotion committed via post-rename stat of the destination, (2) record the success outcome in the caller return value, and (3) remove the remaining staging transaction root (transaction/ directory and any other staging artifacts) so the destination is the sole remaining artifact. If step 3 fails, the repository remains successfully promoted; the workflow shall return a promoted-with-finalization-error result; the staging transaction root shall be preserved when accessible; and cleanup failure must not cause the repository to be misreported as unpromoted. An execution report with completion_status promoted-with-finalization-error and promotion_outcome promoted shall be written to transaction/execution-report.json for diagnostics, recording the promoted destination in its expected_destination field, the preserved staging transaction root in its staging_root field, and the request fingerprint in its request_fingerprint field. Under cleanup failure, the staging-state record shall record the canonical cleanup-failure state: `current_stage` = `success-finalization`, `failed_stage` = `success-finalization`, `completed_stages` includes `promotion` (completed) and does not include `success-finalization` (not completed), `promotion_entered` = `true`, `promotion_outcome` = `promoted`, and `cleanup_failure` = non-empty diagnostic string. The execution report and staging-state record shall agree on the request fingerprint, expected destination, promotion outcome (both `promoted`), failed stage, and terminal result; the two records must not disagree about promotion. No automatic rollback or retry of the failed cleanup operation is authorized.

entries.requirement_text: The promoted repository shall conform to the generated-repository layout contract and the output inventory (product.initializer-output-inventory-v1). Every worktree path must be a fixed worktree file, a material_index entry, or a resolved dynamic family path; no prohibited path may appear. The repository shall contain installed reusable framework material (from material_index entries linked by material_key to the material manifest), product-identified direction material preserved as source evidence (from the direction-evidence dynamic family), an activated product-specification workspace preserved by Level README.md placeholder files, a provenance record, a handoff manifest, and the validated deterministic local Git state whose administrative state (.git/) is governed separately by product.local-git-repository and product.git-bootstrap-profile. Only the repository/ directory inside the staging transaction root shall become the destination; the transaction/ directory and all contents (staging-state, execution-report, validation-report) shall be discarded during success-finalization after promotion commits, in the order: confirm promotion committed, record success, then remove the staging transaction root.

entries.requirement_text: A pre-promotion failure occurs when a required stage fails before promotion begins, or when report finalization fails (including staging-state schema validation failure during in-memory validation, failure to durably write both the validation report and the staging-state record, or failure of the final dual-record consistency verification). When report finalization fails before either record is durably written, the staging transaction root is preserved for diagnostics and neither record claims a written validation result. When only one of the two records has been durably written before the failure, the staging transaction root is preserved for diagnostics including the partially written record; the workflow must not misrepresent a partially written record pair as a consistent finalized outcome. Under pre-promotion failure: the destination remains absent; the staging transaction root is preserved for diagnostics when it exists; the execution report records the failed stage identity and carries promotion_outcome = not-promoted and completion_status = failed; the staging-state record records promotion_outcome as not-promoted; the workflow returns a failure result to the caller; and no automatic retry is authorized. The execution report and staging-state record shall agree on the request fingerprint, expected destination, and promotion outcome.

Success is externally observable when the post-rename stat of the destination confirms the renamed repository exists at the expected path.

entries.requirement_text: A cleanup failure after successful promotion occurs when the post-rename stat confirms the destination, the success outcome is recorded, but removal of the remaining staging transaction root fails. Under cleanup failure: the repository remains successfully promoted at the destination; the workflow does not report clean success to the caller; the workflow returns a distinct promoted-with-finalization-error failure result; the staging transaction root is preserved when possible; cleanup failure must not cause the repository to be misreported as unpromoted; and the staging-state record records the canonical cleanup-failure state: `current_stage` = `success-finalization`, `failed_stage` = `success-finalization`, `completed_stages` includes `promotion` (completed) and does not include `success-finalization` (not completed), `promotion_entered` = `true`, `promotion_outcome` = `promoted`, and `cleanup_failure` = non-empty diagnostic string. No automatic rollback or retry of the failed cleanup operation is authorized. The execution report shall carry `promotion_outcome` = `promoted` and `completion_status` = `promoted-with-finalization-error`, record the promoted destination in `expected_destination`, and record the preserved staging transaction root in `staging_root`; the report shall record promotion as completed and success-finalization as failed. The execution report and staging-state record shall agree on the request fingerprint, expected destination, promotion outcome (both `promoted`), failed stage, and terminal result; the two records must not disagree about promotion.
